After `search_foods` or `search_foods_by_nutrient` returned a food code, or when the user pastes a food-nutrition.canada.ca serving-portion or nutrientReport URL.

food_code.description:
CNF food code (e.g. 61 Milk, fluid, partly skimmed, 2% M.F.; 119 Cheese, cheddar). Give this or `url`.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 99999999.

lang.description:
Language of the description, nutrient names, measure, refuse, yield and source texts.

Provider reference: allowed values ["en", "fr"]; default "en".

measure.description: One of the food's measure names as the CNF writes them (e.g. '250ml', '100ml diced', '1 slice'); spaces, commas and case are ignored. Adds `value_per_measure` to every nutrient row and sets `selected_measure`.

nutrient_ids.description: Return only these CNF nutrient ids (`nutrient_name_id` from `list_nutrients`). An id that is not in the CNF nutrient dictionary is invalid input; a known nutrient the CNF does not report for this food is simply absent.

url.description: A CNF page URL carrying the food code: https://food-nutrition.canada.ca/cnf-fce/serving-portion?id={food_code} or .../nutrientReport-rapportAliment?food-aliment-id={food_code}&id=...

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
The complete Canadian Nutrient File record of one food by `food_code` (or a pasted CNF serving-portion / nutrientReport page URL): description, every nutrient the CNF reports for it per 100 g edible portion, joined with the CNF nutrient dictionary (symbol, INFOODS tagname, unit such as g / mg / µg / IU / kcal, decimals, nutrient group) and the data-source code list (provenance; source 1 marks values changed to meet Canadian fortification regulations), plus the food's serving measures with conversion factors and gram weights, refuse (inedible portion) rows and yield rows. Nutrients the CNF does not report for a food are absent, never zero-filled. `nutrient_ids` restricts the nutrient rows (203 Protein, 208 Energy kcal, 301 Calcium, 339 Vitamin D µg, 324 Vitamin D IU, ...; see `list_nutrients`); `measure` names one of the food's measures (e.g. '250ml') and adds `value_per_measure` to every nutrient row. Seven to eight anonymous GET calls to /api/canadian-nutrient-file/ (food, nutrientamount, servingsize, refuseamount, yieldamount, nutrientname, nutrientgroup, nutrientsource). An unknown food code is `not_found` (the API answers an empty list).

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
Find Canadian Nutrient File foods by name. The CNF API has no server-side search: the function downloads the complete food list (GET /api/canadian-nutrient-file/food/, 5,690 rows, ~470 KB) and matches client-side the way the CNF web app does: case- and accent-insensitive, every word of the query must appear somewhere in the food description, in any order ('apple raw' finds 'Pineapple, raw'). A query that is only digits also matches the food code exactly. Results keep the API's order, are paged with `limit`/`offset` and report `total_matches`; no match is a valid empty result. Each row carries the `food_code` that `get_food` takes and the food's CNF serving-size page URL. `lang` selects English or French descriptions (same food codes).

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
Foods ranked by the amount of one nutrient, optionally within one CNF food group: the CNF web app's 'Search by nutrient' (GET /cnf-fce/newNutrientSearch for the session cookie and CSRF token, then POST /cnf-fce/nutrientSearch-rechercheAliment in the same session; the only food-group aware surface of the CNF). Every matching food comes back with the CNF's chosen portion, its gram weight and the nutrient amount per that portion in the nutrient's unit, sorted by amount descending (or ascending). The web app returns the whole result in one page (e.g. 219 dairy foods for Vitamin D); the function pages it with `limit`/`offset` and reports `total_records` as the page states it. `nutrient_id` must be one of the 152 nutrients the form offers (`list_nutrients`; a different id is `not_found`), `food_group_id` one of the 23 groups or 0 for all (`list_food_groups`). Each row carries the `food_code` for `get_food` and the CNF nutrient-report URL. English only (the form is served in English).

The response contains the tool result directly.
